name: Joplin, MO-KS

nodes.name: Prince of Wales-Hyder Census Area, AK

methods: Data. US Census LEHD LODES 8.5 origin-destination files, 2002–2024, on 2020 census blocks: the main and aux files of MO, KS plus every other state's aux file (residents of these states working there). Each file was checked against its SHA-256 checksum. Flows are aggregated to 2020 tracts inside the 3-county metro (Jasper, Cherokee KS, Newton) and to counties outside it. Only flows of ≥10 workers are drawn.
Job types. Private jobs (JT02) are consistent for 2002–2024. All jobs (JT00) add federal jobs from 2010, and an OPM suppression in 2015 cuts federal jobs by 8.4% in Missouri.

In-state vs out-of-state. In-state means Missouri. Residents of other states (including the Kansas or Illinois side of a metro's own commuter field) are counted as out-of-state when they live outside the metro.
Distance. Straight-line miles between block internal points. The distance-decay β is the exponent of a doubly-constrained gravity model among the metro's tracts (Poisson maximum likelihood).

Commuting communities. Leiden modularity (Traag et al. 2019) on the undirected tract network (pairs ≥3 workers, no self-loops), γ = 1.0. Each year's partition is a consensus over 100 seeds (Lancichinetti & Fortunato 2012). Communities are tracked across years by Jaccard overlap ≥0.3 (Greene et al. 2010).

Job centres. Local Moran's I (LISA) High-High clusters on log job density using 3-year centred means (queen contiguity, 999 permutations, p<0.05). A centre must hold ≥2% of metro jobs and qualify in ≥2 of 3 consecutive years (Arribas-Bel & Sanz-Gracia 2014; Ha et al. 2024).

Flow trends. Each tract or county pair with ≥10 workers on average gets a Hamed–Rao modified Mann–Kendall test with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR (q<0.05). Classes follow Esri's emerging-hot-spot logic: new, intensifying, persistent, declining, fading. Pairs that are neither are left grey.

Caveats. LODES places some workers of multi-site employers at headquarters, so long flows (>100 mi, flagged) can be reporting artefacts (Green et al. 2017). Tract job jumps that revert are reassignments, not real change (flagged tract-years here: 0107.00 in 2007, 0102.00 in 2008, 0107.00 in 2008, 0102.00 in 2009). The residence model changed in 2009, at the same time as the recession. Since 2020, remote workers appear at their employer's address. Out-of-state files are missing for Michigan 2022–24 and a few states in early years.
